summary: Targeted actions no longer pre-select a target: the client clears Core's pre-filled first target and starts on 'Choose a target…'; Confirm (and the alternative-cost review) waits for a pick, movement too. Core publishes HarshChoicesView so the client shows the engine's consequence instead of recounting provinces. Deleted the unused client UnitForce.
validation: Core.Tests built (0 errors); EventDecisionTests HarshQueries and LastProvince pass with the new view assertions; client built (0 errors). Native checks on the final build with ripgrep installed passed: gold-payment (11 modes), movement-ui, support-cards, multi-targets-ui, decision-chooser (all 9 modes, after fixing a regression found by the full sweep: the alternative-cost review let a cost be confirmed with no target). Full sweep of the 52 check-*.sh scripts found 35 passing and 17 failing; 13 of the failures (event-decisions harsh-keep, attack-targets normal, crimson-duel, either-or-ui, persistent-home, player-clarity, shown-cards, stabilization, stat-tokens, table-followup, top-cards-ui, unit-standard, war-room-motion) fail identically on a baseline worktree at the pre-change commit, so they predate this change. NOT yet re-verified on this branch: duel-demo, duel-match and ui-consolidation, which passed on the baseline but failed in the sweep (no clear error; duel-match logged a Godot canvas_map rendering error) and may be flaky under memory pressure; re-runs were stopped by memory-pressure reaps. Not run: full tools/check.sh; visual review of the new picker and Harsh Choices panel.
remaining: Re-run duel-demo, duel-match and ui-consolidation on this branch with more free memory to decide whether they are regressions or flakes. Investigate the 13 baseline-failing captures separately. Visual review of the 'Choose a target…' picker and Harsh Choices panel. No Core 'optional target' flag was added: apart from the Attack family and Slots (Min 0), only Unimpeachable Name has an optional single target and it already offers a separate no-target button.
